title: कर्णालीमा १०औँ राष्ट्रिय खेलकुदको तयारी तीव्र, ३२ खेलमा प्रतिस्पर्धा हुने
content:
No ads found for this position काठमाडौं । कर्णाली प्रदेशमा आयोजना हुन लागेको दसौँ राष्ट्रिय खेलकुद प्रतियोगिताको तयारी अन्तिम चरणमा पुगेको राष्ट्रिय खेलकुद परिषद्ले जनाएको छ। प्रतियोगिताबारे जानकारी दिन परिषद्ले बिहीबार पत्रकारहरूसँग अन्तरक्रिया कार्यक्रम आयोजना गर्दै तयारीका विभिन्न पक्ष सार्वजनिक गरेको हो। राष्ट्रिय खेलकुद परिषद्को १२१औँ बोर्ड बैठकले दसौँ राष्ट्रिय खेलकुद २०८३ मंसिर १६ देखि २७ गतेसम्म सञ्चालन गर्ने निर्णय गरेको छ। प्रतियोगिताको औपचारिक उद्घाटन मंसिर १६ गते सुर्खेतको वीरेन्द्रनगरस्थित कर्णाली प्रदेश रंगशालामा हुनेछ। समापन समारोह पनि मंसिर २७ गते सोही रंगशालामा आयोजना गरिनेछ। प्रतियोगिताका खेलहरू भने मंसिर ८ गतेदेखि नै सुरु हुने परिषद्ले जनाएको छ। प्रतियोगिताअन्तर्गत विभिन्न ३२ खेलका ३८४ विधामा प्रतिस्पर्धा हुनेछ। प्रतियोगितामा सातवटै प्रदेश, नेपाल प्रहरी, नेपाली सेना, सशस्त्र प्रहरी बल (एपीएफ) र गैरआवासीय नेपाली संघ (एनआरएनए) गरी ११ टोलीको सहभागिता रहनेछ। प्रत्येक टोलीबाट ६६० जना सहभागी हुने अनुमान गरिएको छ। जसमा ३१४ महिला र ३४६ पुरुष खेलाडी रहनेछन्। प्रतियोगितामा खेलाडी, प्रशिक्षक, व्यवस्थापक, निर्णायक तथा अन्य प्राविधिकसहित ठूलो संख्यामा जनशक्ति परिचालन हुनेछ। परिषद्का अनुसार प्रतियोगितामा कुल एक हजार ३० जना निर्णायक रहनेछन्। प्रतियोगिताका खेलहरू सुर्खेतमा २३, नेपालगञ्जमा २, बर्दियामा २, दैलेखमा १, कालिकोटमा १, सल्यानमा २ र पश्चिम रुकुममा १ गरी विभिन्न स्थानमा सञ्चालन गरिनेछ। दसौँ राष्ट्रिय खेलकुदमा ३८४ स्वर्ण, ३८४ रजत र ५६९ कांस्य गरी कुल एक हजार ३३७ पदकका लागि प्रतिस्पर्धा हुनेछ। प्रतियोगितामा व्यक्तिगततर्फ स्वर्ण पदक विजेतालाई २० हजार, रजत विजेतालाई १५ हजार र कांस्य विजेतालाई ८ हजार रुपैयाँ पुरस्कार प्रदान गरिनेछ। त्यस्तै, टिमतर्फ स्वर्ण विजेतालाई १५ हजार, रजत विजेतालाई १० हजार र कांस्य विजेतालाई ८ हजार रुपैयाँ पुरस्कारको व्यवस्था गरिएको छ। रजत र कांस्य पदक विजेतालाई पहिलोपटक नगद पुरस्कारको व्यवस्था गरिएको परिषद्ले जनाएको छ। राष्ट्रिय खेलकुद परिषद्ले प्रतियोगितालाई व्यवस्थित र सफल बनाउन आवश्यक तयारी अघि बढाइएको जनाउँदै खेलाडी तथा खेलकर्मीको सहभागितामा राष्ट्रिय खेलकुदको महत्त्वलाई थप प्रभावकारी बनाउने लक्ष्य लिएको छ। Kathmandu. The National Sports Council has stated that preparations for the 10th National Games to be held in Karnali Province have reached the final stage. The council organized an interaction program with journalists on Thursday to provide information about the competition and made various aspects of the preparations public. The 121st board meeting of the National Sports Council has decided to hold the 10th National Games 2083 from Mangsir 16 to 27. The formal inauguration of the competition will be held on Mangsir 16 at the Karnali Province Stadium in Birendranagar, Surkhet. The closing ceremony will also be held at the same stadium on Mangsir 27. The council has stated that the competition will begin on November 21. Under the competition, there will be competition in 384 categories of 32 different sports. Eleven teams from all seven provinces, Nepal Police, Nepal Army, Armed Police Force (APF) and Non-Resident Nepali Association (NRNA) will participate in the competition. It is estimated that 660 people will participate from each team. There will be 314 female and 346 male players. A large number of human resources, including players, coaches, managers, judges and other technicians, will be mobilized for the competition. According to the council, a total of 1,030 judges will be involved in the competition. The tournament games will be held at various locations including 23 in Surkhet, 2 in Nepalgunj, 2 in Bardiya, 1 in Dailekh, 1 in Kalikot, 2 in Salyan, and 1 in West Rukum. A total of 1,337 medals will be competed for in the 10th National Games, including 384 gold, 384 silver, and 569 bronze. In the competition, the individual gold medal winner will be awarded Rs 20,000, the silver winner Rs 15,000, and the bronze winner Rs 8,000. Similarly, the team gold winner will be awarded Rs 15,000, the silver winner Rs 10,000, and the bronze winner Rs 8,000. The council has stated that for the first time, cash prizes have been provided to silver and bronze medal winners. The National Sports Council has stated that necessary preparations have been made to make the competition organized and successful, and has set a goal to make the importance of the National Games more effective with the participation of players and sports personnel.

The National Sports Council has stated that preparations for the 10th National Games to be held in Karnali Province have reached the final stage. The council organized an interaction program with journalists on Thursday to provide information about the competition and made various aspects of the preparations public. The 121st board meeting of the National Sports Council has decided to hold the 10th National Games 2083 from Mangsir 16 to 27. The formal inauguration of the competition will be held on Mangsir 16 at the Karnali Province Stadium in Birendranagar, Surkhet. The closing ceremony will also be held at the same stadium on Mangsir 27. The council has stated that the competition will begin on November 21. Under the competition, there will be competition in 384 categories of 32 different sports. Eleven teams from all seven provinces, Nepal Police, Nepal Army, Armed Police Force (APF) and Non-Resident Nepali Association (NRNA) will participate in the competition. It is estimated that 660 people will participate from each team. There will be 314 female and 346 male players. A large number of human resources, including players, coaches, managers, judges and other technicians, will be mobilized for the competition. According to the council, a total of 1,030 judges will be involved in the competition. The tournament games will be held at various locations including 23 in Surkhet, 2 in Nepalgunj, 2 in Bardiya, 1 in Dailekh, 1 in Kalikot, 2 in Salyan, and 1 in West Rukum. A total of 1,337 medals will be competed for in the 10th National Games, including 384 gold, 384 silver, and 569 bronze. In the competition, the individual gold medal winner will be awarded Rs 20,000, the silver winner Rs 15,000, and the bronze winner Rs 8,000. Similarly, the team gold winner will be awarded Rs 15,000, the silver winner Rs 10,000, and the bronze winner Rs 8,000. The council has stated that for the first time, cash prizes have been provided to silver and bronze medal winners. The National Sports Council has stated that necessary preparations have been made to make the competition organized and successful, and has set a goal to make the importance of the National Games more effective with the participation of players and sports personnel.

प्रतियोगिताका खेलहरू भने मंसिर ८ गतेदेखि नै सुरु हुने परिषद्ले जनाएको छ। प्रतियोगिताअन्तर्गत विभिन्न ३२ खेलका ३८४ विधामा प्रतिस्पर्धा हुनेछ।

प्रतियोगितामा सातवटै प्रदेश, नेपाल प्रहरी, नेपाली सेना, सशस्त्र प्रहरी बल (एपीएफ) र गैरआवासीय नेपाली संघ (एनआरएनए) गरी ११ टोलीको सहभागिता रहनेछ। प्रत्येक टोलीबाट ६६० जना सहभागी हुने अनुमान गरिएको छ।

जसमा ३१४ महिला र ३४६ पुरुष खेलाडी रहनेछन्।

प्रतियोगितामा खेलाडी, प्रशिक्षक, व्यवस्थापक, निर्णायक तथा अन्य प्राविधिकसहित ठूलो संख्यामा जनशक्ति परिचालन हुनेछ। परिषद्का अनुसार प्रतियोगितामा कुल एक हजार ३० जना निर्णायक रहनेछन्।

प्रतियोगिताका खेलहरू सुर्खेतमा २३, नेपालगञ्जमा २, बर्दियामा २, दैलेखमा १, कालिकोटमा १, सल्यानमा २ र पश्चिम रुकुममा १ गरी विभिन्न स्थानमा सञ्चालन गरिनेछ।

दसौँ राष्ट्रिय खेलकुदमा ३८४ स्वर्ण, ३८४ रजत र ५६९ कांस्य गरी कुल एक हजार ३३७ पदकका लागि प्रतिस्पर्धा हुनेछ।

प्रतियोगितामा व्यक्तिगततर्फ स्वर्ण पदक विजेतालाई २० हजार, रजत विजेतालाई १५ हजार र कांस्य विजेतालाई ८ हजार रुपैयाँ पुरस्कार प्रदान गरिनेछ। त्यस्तै, टिमतर्फ स्वर्ण विजेतालाई १५ हजार, रजत विजेतालाई १० हजार र कांस्य विजेतालाई ८ हजार रुपैयाँ पुरस्कारको व्यवस्था गरिएको छ।

रजत र कांस्य पदक विजेतालाई पहिलोपटक नगद पुरस्कारको व्यवस्था गरिएको परिषद्ले जनाएको छ।

राष्ट्रिय खेलकुद परिषद्ले प्रतियोगितालाई व्यवस्थित र सफल बनाउन आवश्यक तयारी अघि बढाइएको जनाउँदै खेलाडी तथा खेलकर्मीको सहभागितामा राष्ट्रिय खेलकुदको महत्त्वलाई थप प्रभावकारी बनाउने लक्ष्य लिएको छ।

Kathmandu. The National Sports Council has stated that preparations for the 10th National Games to be held in Karnali Province have reached the final stage. The council organized an interaction program with journalists on Thursday to provide information about the competition and made various aspects of the preparations public. The 121st board meeting of the National Sports Council has decided to hold the 10th National Games 2083 from Mangsir 16 to 27. The formal inauguration of the competition will be held on Mangsir 16 at the Karnali Province Stadium in Birendranagar, Surkhet. The closing ceremony will also be held at the same stadium on Mangsir 27. The council has stated that the competition will begin on November 21. Under the competition, there will be competition in 384 categories of 32 different sports. Eleven teams from all seven provinces, Nepal Police, Nepal Army, Armed Police Force (APF) and Non-Resident Nepali Association (NRNA) will participate in the competition. It is estimated that 660 people will participate from each team. There will be 314 female and 346 male players. A large number of human resources, including players, coaches, managers, judges and other technicians, will be mobilized for the competition. According to the council, a total of 1,030 judges will be involved in the competition. The tournament games will be held at various locations including 23 in Surkhet, 2 in Nepalgunj, 2 in Bardiya, 1 in Dailekh, 1 in Kalikot, 2 in Salyan, and 1 in West Rukum. A total of 1,337 medals will be competed for in the 10th National Games, including 384 gold, 384 silver, and 569 bronze. In the competition, the individual gold medal winner will be awarded Rs 20,000, the silver winner Rs 15,000, and the bronze winner Rs 8,000. Similarly, the team gold winner will be awarded Rs 15,000, the silver winner Rs 10,000, and the bronze winner Rs 8,000. The council has stated that for the first time, cash prizes have been provided to silver and bronze medal winners. The National Sports Council has stated that necessary preparations have been made to make the competition organized and successful, and has set a goal to make the importance of the National Games more effective with the participation of players and sports personnel.
